ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, within the quadrilateral $ABCD$, points E and F are the midpoints of sides AD and BC, respectively. Extend CD to point G such that DG=CD. Construct quadrilateral $DGME$ outside of quadrilateral $ABCD$ using DG and DE as sides. Connect BM to intersect AD at point N, and connect FN. If DG=DE=1 and $\angle ADC=60^\circ$, what is the length of FN?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure: connect EF, AF\\
$\because$ quadrilateral $DGME$, $DG=CD=1$,\\
$\therefore$ $DC\parallel EF$,\\
$\because$ $\angle ADC=60^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle AEF=60^\circ$\\
$\because$ points E, F are the midpoints of sides AD, BC respectively\\
$\therefore$ $AB\parallel EF$, $AE=DE$\\
$\therefore$ Quadrilateral ABFE is a parallelogram, $\angle BAN=\angle MEN$\\
$\because$ $DG=DC$, $DG=DE$\\
$\therefore$ $AE=EF=AB=ME=1$\\
$\because$ $\angle AEF=60^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle AEF$ is an equilateral triangle\\
In $\triangle ABN$ and $\triangle EMN$\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
ME=AB \\
\angle MEN=\angle BAN \\
\angle MNE=\angle ANB
\end{array}\right.$\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle ABN \cong \triangle EMN$ (by SAA)\\
$\therefore$ $AN=NE$\\
$\therefore$ $NE=\frac{1}{2}AE=\frac{1}{2}$\\
$\therefore$ $FN\perp AE$\\
$\therefore$ $FN=\sqrt{1^2-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2}=\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, ABCD is drawn as an obliquely placed parallelogram, AB is parallel to DC, and AD is parallel to BC; E is on AD, and F is on BC; G, D, C are on the same straight line, with G on the left side of D; DGME is a parallelogram located outside ABCD, and side DG is adjacent to DE; BM intersects AD at N, and FN is drawn. Reasoning: Connect EF and AF according to the figure. Because E and F are respectively the midpoints of the two opposite sides AD and BC of parallelogram ABCD, EF ∥ AB ∥ DC, and EF=AB=DC. Also DG=CD=1, so EF=1. Because E is the midpoint of AD, and DE=1, AE=DE=1. In the outside parallelogram DGME, ME=DG=1, and ME ∥ DG ∥ DC. From ∠ADC=60°, combined with AE and DE being collinear and EF ∥ DC, it can be obtained that ∠AEF=60°. Therefore in triangle AEF, AE=EF=1 and the included angle is 60°, so △AEF is an equilateral triangle. Then compare △ABN and △EMN: AB=ME=1; because AB ∥ ME, and A, N, E are collinear, ∠BAN=∠MEN; BM intersects AD at N, so ∠ANB=∠MNE are vertical angles. Therefore △ABN≅△EMN, obtaining AN=NE. Thus N is the midpoint of AE, NE=AE/2=1/2. In equilateral triangle AEF, the line segment FN from vertex F to the midpoint N of base AE is the altitude, so FN=√(1^2-(1/2)^2)=√3/2.
